question: Which metal is placed at the starting of the reactivity series?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **reactivity series**, also known as the **activity series**, is an empirical, calculated, and analytically hierarchical arrangement of metals in **descending order** of their chemical reactivity.
 
• **Potassium** (chemical symbol **K**, **atomic number 19**) is placed at the **top or the starting** of this series because it is the **most reactive** metal among the common elements.
 
• Metals at the top of the series, such as **Potassium** and **Sodium**, lose their **valence electrons** very easily to form **positive ions** (cations), making them highly electropositive.
 
• Because of its extreme reactivity, **Potassium** reacts **violently** even with **cold water** to produce **hydrogen gas** and **potassium hydroxide**, releasing enough heat to ignite the hydrogen. ***Hence, statement 3 is the correct option.***
 
• In contrast, **Aluminium** is placed lower than **Potassium**, **Sodium**, and **Magnesium**. **Iron** is situated in the middle of the series, and **Gold** is located at the very bottom as it is one of the **least reactive** metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Displacement Reactions:** A fundamental application of the **reactivity series** is predicting **displacement reactions**, where a **more reactive metal** (like **Potassium** or **Zinc**) will displace a **less reactive metal** (like **Copper** or **Silver**) from its salt solution.
 
• **Reaction with Water and Acids:** 
 
 
• Metals like **Potassium**, **Sodium**, and **Calcium** react with **cold water**.
 
• Metals like **Magnesium** react with **hot water**.
 
• Metals like **Aluminium**, **Zinc**, and **Iron** react only with **steam**.
 
• **Gold**, **Silver**, and **Platinum** do not react with water or dilute acids at all.
 
 
 
• **Extraction Methods:** The position in the series determines the **extraction process**. Metals at the top (**Potassium** to **Aluminium**) are extracted via **electrolysis** of their molten ores. Metals in the middle (**Zinc** to **Lead**) are reduced using **carbon** (coke). Metals at the bottom (**Gold** and **Silver**) are often found in their **native state** in nature.
 
• **Noble Metals:** **Gold** (**Au**) and **Platinum** (**Pt**) are referred to as **noble metals** because they remain unaffected by air, moisture, and most acidic reagents, which is why they are used in **jewelry** and **electronics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Storage of Reactive Metals:** Due to their high affinity for **oxygen** and **moisture**, **Potassium** and **Sodium** are stored under **kerosene oil** to prevent **accidental fires** or oxidation in the open air.
 
• **Hydrogen Reference:** Although it is a non-metal, **Hydrogen** is included in the reactivity series to serve as a **reference point**. Metals placed **above hydrogen** can displace it from **dilute acids** to form **hydrogen gas**, while those below it cannot.
 
• **Order of the Series (Descending):** **Potassium** > **Sodium** > **Calcium** > **Magnesium** > **Aluminium** > **Zinc** > **Iron** > **Tin** > **Lead** > **[Hydrogen]** > **Copper** > **Mercury** > **Silver** > **Gold**.
 
• **Chemical Symbols and Atomic Numbers:** 
 
 
• **Potassium (K):** **19**
 
• **Aluminium (Al):** **13**
 
• **Iron (Fe):** **26**
 
• **Gold (Au):** **79**
